chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The broken [stone] and the flat [stone] are thrown on their behalf. He said: "And the children are thrown on their behalf."
ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for the stones used in ramy and for children during Hajj?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the technical validity of the Jamarat ritual, emphasizing that minor imperfections in the pebbles do not invalidate the act. It further extends the concession of *wakalah* (delegation) to children, reflecting the Shia juristic view that their guardians may perform the rite on their behalf until they reach maturity, ensuring the completeness of the Hajj obligations.
